# Base image with OpenMPI, Flux, and AWS EFA support for ARM64
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installs
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, clone, build, and install LAMMPS
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential \
        ca-certificates \
        cmake \
        git && \
    # Clone the latest version of the LAMMPS source code
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /tmp/lammps && \
    cd /tmp/lammps && \
    # Create a build directory
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake
    # - Enable MPI support
    # - Specify MPI C++ and C compilers
    # - Enable the REAXFF package as required
    # - Set install prefix to a system path location
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
      -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
      -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=mpicxx \
      -D CMAKE_C_COMPILER=mpicc \
      -D PKG_REAXFF=ON \
      ../cmake && \
    # Build LAMMPS using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Install the lmp executable to /usr/local/bin
    make install && \
    # Verify that the 'lmp' executable is in the system PATH
    which lmp && \
    # Create a workspace directory for the application examples
    mkdir -p /opt/lammps-reax-workspace && \
    # Copy the required example files into the workspace
    # This is done from the cloned source before it's removed
    cp /tmp/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /opt/lammps-reax-workspace/ && \
    # Clean up to reduce image size
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/lammps && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the final working directory to the location of the example files
WORKDIR /opt/lammps-reax-workspace

# MiniCluster manifest for a LAMMPS experiment on AWS ARM CPU instances
# This configuration is designed for the Flux Operator to schedule a parallel job.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name for the MiniCluster instance
  name: lammps-reax-hns-aws-arm
  # Deploy to the default namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 for the single-node test case.
  size: 1
  # The maximum number of pods the MiniCluster can scale to.
  maxSize: 4
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run across the cluster.
  tasks: 8

  # Do not delete pods after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging verbosity settings.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux Operator specific configurations
  flux:
    # Set the architecture to ARM for AWS Graviton instances.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use a Flux view container image built for ARM architecture.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Run the flux broker in the main application container, not a sidecar.
      disable: true

  # Defines the main application container for the job.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed by Flux. "flux run" is prepended by the operator.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # Ensure the latest version of the container is used for experiments.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # This container is a worker, not the one that launches the MiniCluster. This MUST be false.
      launcher: false
      # Resource requests for AWS-specific hardware (Elastic Fabric Adapter).
      # No CPU or memory limits are set, allowing the pod to be Burstable.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

updates.reason: The previous run used only 1 node and 8 tasks, which is severe underutilization. This run scales up to the maximum allowed 4 nodes, using all 64 cores on each node (256 tasks total) and increases the problem size proportionally to maximize the Figure of Merit through weak scaling.

The previous run scaled to the maximum of 4 nodes and 256 tasks, achieving a strong FOM of 744.912. This attempt aims to further optimize by doubling the problem size (`-v x 16 -v y 8 -v z 4`) on the same hardware. This increases the atoms-per-task, which can improve the computation-to-communication ratio and potentially lead to a higher FOM without exceeding memory limits.

Performance peaked at 744.912 atom steps/sec in the second attempt with 4 nodes, 256 tasks, and a problem size multiplier of `x=8, y=8, z=4`. The third attempt, which increased the problem size (`x=16`), resulted in a catastrophic performance drop to 1.158. This indicates that memory, cache, or communication limits were exceeded. The optimal configuration has been found.

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-hns-aws-arm
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 16 -v y 8 -v z 4 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      disable: true
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  maxSize: 4
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
  size: 4
  tasks: 256

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile lammps setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH and run which lmp to ensure success.
You MUST build LAMMPS for a multi-node MPI environment

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, *atom steps per second.  It could be Matom or katom.
You MUST choose the largest problem size to maximize FOM. You MAY go up to 4 nodes. 
You MUST make an effort to increase problem size as much as you can.
context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3). You are limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.testing: Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite for testing only on all processes of one node.
context.details:
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
